questions.question: Motion of an object is __________ if its velocity is constant.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**uniform**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• It is known as uniform motion when an object moves in a straight path as direction remains constant at a constant speed.
 
• This indicates that the body's velocity stays constant as it travels the same distance in the same amount of time.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__** 

Non-Uniform Motion:

 
• When an object travels at varying speeds and does not cover the same distance in a constant amount of time.

Speed:

 
• Speed is a change in an object's location in any direction.
 
• Speed is also defined as the ratio of distance to the amount of time it took to cover that distance. 

Direction:

 
• Direction is characterized as the course that anything follows. 
 
• The route that must be taken to go to a particular location. 
 
• The direction in which something is beginning to take shape, or the direction you are facing.

questions.question: The motion of a swing is an example of _______ motion.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**oscillatory**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Oscillation** is the repetitive or** periodic variation**, typically in time, of some measure about a central value or between two or more different states.
 
• Familiar examples of oscillation include a **swinging pendulum **and **alternating current.**
 
• Oscillations occur not only in **mechanical systems** but also in dynamic systems in virtually every area of science: for example, the beating of the **human heart (for circulation),** business **cycles **in economics,** predator-prey population **cycles in ecology, **geothermal geysers **in geology, vibration of strings in guitar and other string instruments, the periodic firing of nerve cells in the brain, and the periodic swelling of Cepheid variable star in **astronomy.**
 
• The term vibration is precisely used to** describe a mechanical oscillation.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**** Rectilinear**

 
• Linear motion also called** rectilinear motion**, is** one-dimensional** motion along a straight line, and can therefore be described **mathematically using** only one **spatial dimension.**
 
• Linear motion can be of two types:** uniform linear motion**, with constant velocity; and **non-uniform linear motion,** with variable velocity.

** Curvilinear**

 
• The motion of an object moving in a **curved path** is called **curvilinear motion.**
 
• Example: A stone** thrown into the air at an angle**.
 
• The curvilinear motion **describes **the motion of a moving particle that conforms to a known or **fixed curve.**

** Rotatory**

 
• Rotatory motion is the motion that occurs when a** body rotates on its own axis.**
 
• A few examples of rotatory motion are as follows: The motion of the** earth about** its own axis around the sun is an example of rotary motion.

questions.question:
Read the following statements:

Statement 1: The motion of a pendulum is periodic.

Statement 2: The distance-time graph of an object moving with uniform speed is a straight line.

Statement 3: The distance-time graph of an object moving with variable speed is a curved line.

Statement 4: The slope of the distance-time graph indicates the acceleration of the object.

options.text: Statements 1, 2, and 3 are true; 4 is false.
Statements 1 and 4 are true; 2 and 3 are false.
Statements 1, 2, and 4 are true; 3 is false.

questions.solution:
__**CONCEPT**__:

**Periodic Motion and Distance-Time Graphs**

__
 
• **Periodic Motion:** Motion that repeats at regular intervals, such as the motion of a pendulum.
 
• **Distance-Time Graph for Uniform Speed:** A straight line indicating constant speed.
 
• **Distance-Time Graph for Variable Speed:** A curved line indicating changing speed.
 
• **Slope of Distance-Time Graph:** The slope represents speed, not acceleration. Acceleration is the rate of change of velocity, which would be represented on a velocity-time graph.

**Explanation:-__**

 
• **Statement 1:** The motion of a pendulum is periodic.** This is true** because a pendulum repeats its motion at regular intervals.
 
• **Statement 2:** The distance-time graph of an object moving with uniform speed is a straight line. **This is true** because uniform speed implies a constant rate of distance covered per unit time.
 
• **Statement 3:** The distance-time graph of an object moving with variable speed is a curved line. This is true because a curved graph indicates varying speed over time.
 
• **Statement 4:** The slope of the distance-time graph indicates the acceleration of the object. This is **false because the slope of a distance-time graph indicates speed**, not acceleration. Acceleration is indicated by the slope of a velocity-time graph.

**The correct option is 2) Statements 1, 2, and 3 are true; 4 is false**

questions.question: What is the momentum p, of an object of mass m, moving with a velocity ?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**p = mv**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Momentum is a fundamental concept in physics, defined as the product of an object's mass and its velocity.
 
• The formula for momentum (p) is given by p = mv, where m is the mass of the object and v is its velocity.
 
• Momentum is a vector quantity, meaning it has both magnitude and direction, aligning with the direction of the object's velocity.
 
• In classical mechanics, the conservation of momentum is a crucial principle, stating that the total momentum of a closed system remains constant if no external forces act on it.
 
• The SI unit of momentum is kilogram meter per second (kg·m/s).

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Impulse:**

 
 
• Impulse is the change in momentum of an object when a force is applied over a time interval.
 
• It is calculated as the product of the force (F) and the time (∆t) during which the force acts, given by Impulse = F∆t.
 
• Impulse has the same unit as momentum (kg·m/s) and is also a vector quantity.
 
 
 
• **Newton's Second Law:**
 
 
• Newton's Second Law of Motion states that the force acting on an object is equal to the rate of change of its momentum, F = dp/dt.
 
• This law forms the basis for the relationship between force, mass, and acceleration.
 
 
 
• **Conservation of Momentum:**
 
 
• The principle of conservation of momentum states that in a closed system with no external forces, the total momentum before and after an event remains constant.
 
• This principle is widely used in collision and explosion problems in physics.
 
 
 
• **Elastic and Inelastic Collisions:**
 
 
• In an elastic collision, both momentum and kinetic energy are conserved.
 
• In an inelastic collision, momentum is conserved, but kinetic energy is not; some of the kinetic energy is converted into other forms of energy, such as heat or sound.

questions.question: With an initial velocity of 10 m/s, an object is thrown vertically upwards. The maximum height attained by the object is (Assume g = 10m/s²)
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**5 m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• When an object is thrown vertically upwards, it decelerates under the influence of gravity (g = 10 m/s²).
 
• The initial velocity (u) of the object is given as 10 m/s.
 
• At the maximum height, the final velocity (v) is 0 m/s.
 
• Using the equation of motion: v²=u²-2gh, we can calculate the maximum height (h).
 
• Substituting the values, 0=10²-2times 10times h, solving this gives h=5m meters.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Equations of Motion**

 
 
• These are used to describe the relationship between the velocity, acceleration, and displacement of an object.
 
• The three primary equations of motion are: v=u+at, s=ut+(1)/(2)at², and v²=u²+2as.
 
 
 
• **Gravitational Acceleration (g)**
 
 
• It is the acceleration due to gravity, typically taken as 9.8 m/s² or approximated to 10 m/s² for simplicity in calculations.
 
• This value indicates how fast an object accelerates when falling freely under the influence of gravity.
 
 
 
• **Maximum Height of a Projectile**
 
 
• The maximum height is the highest point reached by an object projected upwards.
 
• At this point, the vertical component of the object's velocity is zero.
 
 
 
• **Vertical Projectile Motion**
 
 
• When an object is projected vertically upwards, it moves against the gravity until it reaches a point where the velocity becomes zero.
 
• It then starts descending under the influence of gravity, retracing its path.

__
 
• **Rockets work **on the principle of **conservation of Momentum**, which is derived from Newton's third law of motion.
 
• **The rocket expels mass (propellant) at high speed, and in turn, the rocket moves in the opposite direction.**
 
• In a rocket, gasses at high temperatures and pressure are created by the combustion of fuel.
 
• They escape with a high constant velocity via a nozzle.
 
• The large, backward momentum of the gasses gives the rocket an equal forward momentum.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Conservation of Momentum: According to this principle, in an isolated system, the vector sum of linear momenta of all bodies of a system is conserved and is not affected due to their mutual action and reaction.
 
• If two bodies of different masses collide with each other and there is no external force acting on it them,
 
• The initial momentum of bodies = Final momentum of bodies

questions.question: The rate of change in the velocity of an object per unit time is referred as ________.

__
 
• The rate of change in the velocity of an object per unit time is referred as** acceleration.**
 
• When the velocity of a moving object changes either in magnitude or in direction or in both, then the body is said to be in acceleration.
 
• The rate of change in velocity is called acceleration.
 
• ⇒ a =(Δ v)/(Δ t)
 
• Where Δv = change in velocity/speed and Δt = time

questions.question: Which among the following is*** not*** an example of straight line motion?
questions.solution:
__**Concept:**__

**Motion and Its Types **

__
 
• Motion is the change in the position of an object with time. 
 
• Examples of motion include a flying bird, a moving car, a running boy, a child sliding, motion of spinning top etc.
 
• There are different types of motion. Some of them are Straight line motion, circular motion, periodic motion, vibratory motion and rotatory motion. 

**Straight Line Motion**

 
• The motion which is confined to a straight line is known as straight-line motion. 
 
• A car is moving on a straight road, or a train moving on a straight railway track are examples of straight-line motion. 
 
• A child sliding on a slide is also a straight line motion. Though the slide is inclined, it is like a straight line and the boy moving on it is in straight-line motion. 
 
• A giant wheel can be seen in fairs or carnivals. It rotates in a circular direction. It is an example of circular motion. 

**Conclusion:**__

__
 
• Examples of straight line motion among the options are A child sliding on the slide, Car moving on a straight track.
 
• Motion of a giant wheel is an example of circular motion and not straight line motion, so it is the correct option here. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

questions.question: Which of the following is an example of an oscillatory motion?

options.text: Moving of an object in a straight line
Moving of a bus in a circular path
To and fro motion of a simple pendulum
Dropping of an object from a height

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**To and fro motion of a simple pendulum.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__****Oscillatory motion**

__
 
• **​**The** to-and-fro **movement of an object from its mean position is referred to as oscillatory motion.
 
• In a perfect world, the object would be able to oscillate indefinitely without encountering any** friction**; however, in the real world, this is not possible, and the object must come to an** equilibrium.**
 
• **Examples** of oscillatory motion are as follows:
 
 
• Oscillation of **simple pendulum**
 
• **Vibrating strings** of musical instruments are a mechanical example of oscillatory motion
 
• Movement of **spring**
 
• **Alternating current** is an electrical example of oscillatory motion
 
• A series of oscillations are seen in** the cosmological model**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__****Simple Harmonic Motion**

 
• A type of oscillatory motion known as simple harmonic motion (SHM) is defined as a particle moving along a** straight line** at an acceleration that is** inversely proportional **to the distance from a fixed point on the line.
 
• A **restoring force** that complies with **Hooke's law** is required to bring any simple mechanical harmonic system (such as the weight hanging from the spring to the wall) back to its **equilibrium position.**
 
• There are two types of **Simple Harmonic Motion (SHM):**
 
 
• **Linear SHM**: Simple harmonic motion is referred to as linear when a particle moves in a **straight line** around a fixed point (called equilibrium position).
 
• **Angular SHM**: An angular simple harmonic motion occurs when a system moves **long and angularly** with respect to a fixed axis.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Given, u=0 (u=initial velocity), v= 6m/s (v= final velocity), t= 30s (t= time taken) **

 
 
• **Now, we know v= u + at (Where, a= acceleration)**
 
• **x = {{v-u} over t}**
 
• **x = {{6-0} over 30} = 0.2 m/s². **
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **When a body is moving along a straight line with uniform acceleration**, there are relations between velocity, acceleration and distance travelled by the body in a particular time interval known as the **equation of motion.**
 
• **There are three equations of motion:**
 
 
• v = u + at
 
• s = ut + 1over 2 at²
 
• v² - u² = 2as
 
• Where, u= initial velocity, v= final velocity, a= acceleration, t= time and s= distance.
 
 
 
• If an object starts from rest, **then u= 0.**
 
• If an object comes to rest then **v= 0**.
 
• If an object moves with uniform velocity, its acceleration,** a= 0. **

questions.question:
The distance - time graph for the motion of two vehicles A and B is given below. Which of the following statements is true ?

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cdad6bacc7ad2bb3f224e9f0662208b1f1a28dbd90b5216b300359d4c3cf854c.png]

options.text: Both A and B are moving at the same speed
It is not possible to find out the relative speed of A and B from the graph

questions.solution:
__Concept__:

__
 
• Distance: The path length between two points is called distance.
 
• Speed (v): The rate of change in distance is called speed.
 
• Distance vs time graph: The slope of the distance-time curve represents gives speed.

Slope (m) = tanθ

The slope of distance-time curve = speed (v) = tanθ 

Distance Time Graph

 
• The distance-time graph represents distance v/s time. 
 
• The straight line of the graph means the slope or rate of the graph is constant. 
 
• The slope of the distance-time graph is speed, so a straight line means constant acceleration. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/794f5beae2fab24455b3d3f6c1ef856a33688a76312856ecfad5a3b262c57fd8.png] 

If it is not a straight line, the acceleration is non - uniform. 

Explanation:__

__
 
• The slope of the graph represents the speed of the graph. 
 
• More is the slope, or the angle made by a graph with the time axis, more is the speed. 
 
• From the given graph in the question, the slope of A is more than B.
 
• So, the speed of A is more than the speed of B. __

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/cdad6bacc7ad2bb3f224e9f0662208b1f1a28dbd90b5216b300359d4c3cf854c.png]

questions.question: A body is thrown up and it reaches a height of 5m and then falls down, the total displacement and the total distance covered by the body respectively would be:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**0m, 10m**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Displacement** is the shortest distance between the initial and final position of the body.
 
• **Total displacement** is 0m because the body returns to its starting point.
 
• **Distance** is the total path covered by the body.
 
• **Total distance** covered is 10m, as it travels 5m up and 5m down.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Displacement vs Distance**

 
 
• **Displacement** is a vector quantity with both magnitude and direction.
 
• **Distance** is a scalar quantity and only considers the magnitude.
 
 
 
• **Free Fall**
 
 
• It is the motion of a body where gravity is the only force acting upon it.
 
• In free fall, the body gains speed as it descends.
 
 
 
• **Projectile Motion**
 
 
• It involves objects thrown into the air, affected by gravity and air resistance.
 
• The motion can be analyzed in two dimensions: horizontal and vertical.
 
 
 
• **Acceleration Due to Gravity**
 
 
• The acceleration experienced by an object due to Earth's gravitational pull is approximately 9.8 m/s².
 
• This value remains constant near the surface of the Earth.

questions.question: If the distance time graph of the motion of an object is a straight line but not parallel to the time axis, then it may be concluded that the object is moving with a:
questions.solution:
The correct answer is option 4, i.e. **__constant velocity__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/8c37b42bb84b902f99877c2b1e69a981d2bd4bffaeb6447cb84cc807bcaa2053.png] 

 
• The change in the position of an object with time can be represented on the distance-time graph
 
• when an object travels **equal distances in equal intervals of time, **it moves with **uniform speed. **
 
• This shows that the distance travelled by the object is directly proportional to the time taken.
 
• Thus, for uniform speed, a graph of distance travelled against time is a straight line.
 
• **If this straight line is parallel to the time axis it means the object is at the rest.**
 
• **But if the line is a straight line not parallel to the time axis then the object has no acceleration and therefore it is moving with a "constant velocity".**

questions.question: Uniform circular motion is described by which of the following examples?

options.text: A rain drop falling from the sky
A car moving on a straight road
A monkey jumping from one tree to another

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**motion of clock hands**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Uniform circular motion refers to motion in a circular path with constant speed.
 
• The motion of the hands of a clock is an example of uniform circular motion because they move in a circular path at a constant speed.
 
• The second, minute, and hour hands of a clock each complete a full circle in 60 seconds, 60 minutes, and 12 hours respectively.
 
• Uniform circular motion is characterized by a constant angular velocity.
 
• Even though the speed is constant, the direction of motion is continuously changing, meaning there is a centripetal acceleration directed towards the center of the circular path.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Non-Uniform Circular Motion**

 
 
• In this type of motion, the speed varies while the object moves along a circular path.
 
• Examples include a car turning on a curved road at varying speeds.
 
 
 
• **Linear Motion**
 
 
• In linear motion, an object moves along a straight path.
 
• Examples include a car moving on a straight road or a raindrop falling vertically.
 
 
 
• **Projectile Motion**
 
 
• Projectile motion involves an object moving in a curved trajectory under the influence of gravity.
 
• An example is a monkey jumping from one tree to another.

questions.question: The motion of a particle of mass m is described by the relation, y = ut - 1⁄2 gt2, where u is the initial velocity of the particle. The force acting on the particle is
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**F = - mg**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The motion of a particle of mass m is described by the relation, y = ut - 1⁄2 gt2, where u is the initial velocity of the particle.
 
• The force acting on the particle is given by:
 
 
• **F = - mg**
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **​Newton’s Laws of Motion:**

 
 
• **According to the first law of motion**, "An object at rest will remain at rest and an object moving with uniform velocity will continue to continue with uniform velocity unless we apply an external force on it."

 
 
• For example, a car moving with some velocity will continue to move until we apply brakes to stop it. A ball kept on the road will remain at rest unless we apply some force to move it.
 
 
 
• **According to Newton's second law of motion**, "The rate of change of momentum of any object is directly proportional to the direction of the force applied on the object."
 
• **Newton's third law of motion states that**: "For every action there is always an equal and opposite reaction".
